questions.prompt: Why does the fixed commit have a different id?
options: The id is a hash of the commit's content, including the message. A commit cannot change, so git made a new commit and moved main to it
Git renumbers every commit in the repository whenever history changes
Only the date changed; fixing the message alone would have kept the id
Ids are random and change on every git command

questions.prompt: What happened to the commit with the typo?
options: It still exists, but no branch points to it, so the log no longer lists it
Git deleted it the moment the amend finished
It became the parent of the new commit
It was moved onto a backup branch

questions.prompt: Which commit is the parent of the new commit?
How does this differ from reverting the typo commit?
options: A revert adds a new commit on top and keeps the old one in history; the amend replaced the tip with a new commit
There is no difference; revert and amend both edit the old commit
A revert would have fixed the message without changing any id
A revert deletes the old commit; the amend keeps it

goals.label: Replace the last commit with git commit --amend, keeping its parent
Answer: the parent of the new commit
